evidenceAudit.scope: Primary health centre doctors, nurses and allied health staff in Saudi Arabia screening adults aged 65 years and over for frailty, assessing those who screen positive, and building a care plan covering medicines review, exercise, nutrition, treatable causes of fatigue and weight loss, and referral to a geriatrician. Uses the International Conference of Frailty and Sarcopenia Research (ICFSR) guideline and a 2026 Saudi validation of the Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale. Not for acute illness or end-of-life care planning.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Health Council frailty guideline was found; the pathway follows the ICFSR international guideline and Saudi data are descriptive only.

The ICFSR guideline rates the evidence for screening as low certainty and says systematic screening of all older adults is not clearly supported; it still recommends offering screening to adults 65 and over (Recommendation 1).

The scoring bands of the Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale (cut-off scores for fit, vulnerable and mild, moderate or severe frailty) were not read; only the category names and the Saudi category counts are used.

The Fried phenotype cut-off values for grip strength, walking speed and physical activity (sex- and body-size-adjusted) are not given in the guideline text read and are not written; use the validated instrument's own cut-offs.
The guideline gives no frequency, intensity or duration for exercise (it says the evidence is insufficient), so no exercise prescription numbers are written.
The guideline recommends no medicine to treat frailty, so no regimen is written; the vitamin D recommendation is only for proven deficiency and no vitamin D product dose was verified from a label.
STOPP/START, Beers or STOPPFrail were not opened; the topic names them as the ICFSR-recommended deprescribing tools without listing their criteria.
Figures were read by automated extraction of article text; spot-check each figure against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Frailty is a state of increasing vulnerability caused by decline of reserves in several physiological systems (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 1). Physical frailty is identified by three or more of five components: weakness (low grip strength), slowness (slow walking speed), shrinking (unintentional weight loss), exhaustion and low physical activity; one or two components is pre-frailty (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2). Frailty is linked to falls, polypharmacy, sarcopenia, cognitive decline, hospital admission, institutionalisation and death (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 1). Frailty must be separated from multimorbidity and disability because management differs (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2). Exhaustion is often the first frailty feature to appear, and its causes include depression, sleep apnoea, vitamin B12 deficiency, hypothyroidism, anaemia and hypotension (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).

symptoms: Tiredness or exhaustion, the most common first feature (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).
Unintentional weight loss, which is usually the last of the five phenotype components to appear (ICFSR frailty guideline, Section What is Physical Frailty).
Weakness, slow walking and reduced physical activity (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2).
Falls in the previous 12 months: 20.3% of 182 Saudi community-dwelling older adults reported 1 to 2 falls and 3.8% reported 3 or more (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 3).
physicalSigns: Low grip strength on a dynamometer (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2).
Slow gait speed (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2).
Weight loss and low body mass on measurement (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).
Postural hypotension, which can cause exhaustion (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).
redFlags: Advanced (severe) frailty: refer to a geriatrician where appropriate (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 4).
Unintentional weight loss or undernutrition: look for treatable causes and consider nutrition support (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 7).
Five or more regular medicines, found in 59% of frail older people in pooled data: review and deprescribe (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).
Falls in the last 12 months: assess falls risk as part of the care plan (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 1).
Depression or suspected cognitive impairment: assess and treat (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).
precipitants: Age 60 and over; the pooled Middle East prevalence was 35% frail and 39% pre-frail (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 1).
Chronic diseases such as diabetes, arthritis and cardiovascular disease (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 1).
Undernutrition, depression and low socioeconomic status (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 1).
Rapid ageing of the Saudi population, projected to reach 22.9% aged 65 and over by 2050 (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Several chronic diseases with intact reserve and function; managed disease by disease (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2).
Loss of ability in daily activities; may exist without frailty (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2).
Loss of muscle mass and strength; closely linked and often managed together with frailty (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).

differentials.condition: Depression, anaemia, hypothyroidism or B12 deficiency
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Treatable causes of exhaustion that mimic or worsen frailty (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).
Cognitive decline is a frailty correlate and needs separate assessment (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 1).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Higher total score in the vulnerable to severe categories
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Validated in 182 Saudi adults aged 60 and over; test-retest reliability 0.89 (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 3).

clinicalManagement.title: Offer frailty screening
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At any primary care contact for adults aged 65 and over
actions: Offer opportunistic screening to every adult aged 65 or over using a simple validated instrument suited to the clinic (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 1).
Use the Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale where a validated Arabic instrument is needed (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 3).
Make sure staff are trained to screen (ICFSR frailty guideline, Section Who should conduct frailty screening).

clinicalManagement.title: Assess those who screen positive
actions: Assess the five Fried phenotype components and classify as frail (three or more) or pre-frail (one or two) (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2).
Separate frailty from multimorbidity and disability (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2).
Check grip strength and gait speed (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 3).

clinicalManagement.title: Look for treatable causes
actions: Check for depression, anaemia, hypotension, hypothyroidism and vitamin B12 deficiency as causes of exhaustion (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).
Look for treatable causes of weight loss and diagnose undernutrition formally (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 7).

clinicalManagement.title: Agree a care plan
actions: Write a care plan in line with the person's preferences, goals and level of frailty (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).
Review all medicines and deprescribe using standard tools such as STOPP or the Beers criteria (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).
Offer a multicomponent physical activity programme with progressive resistance training (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 5 and 6).
Consider protein or calorie supplementation if weight loss or undernutrition is diagnosed, paired with exercise (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 7 and 8).
Advise on oral health and offer social support for unmet needs (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 9 and 14).

clinicalManagement.title: Refer when needed
actions: Refer to a geriatrician where frailty is advanced (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 4).
Consider home-based training where attendance is difficult (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 15).

clinicalManagement.title: Review
actions: Re-assess function, weight, medicines and goals; adjust the care plan (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 3).

medicationPlan.note: No medicine is recommended to treat frailty itself: the ICFSR guideline states that pharmacological treatment as presently available is not recommended (Recommendation 10), hormone therapy is not recommended (Recommendation 13), and vitamin D is not recommended unless deficiency is present (Recommendation 11). Medicine work in this topic is review and deprescribing of existing medicines, and treatment of the specific causes found (for example anaemia, hypothyroidism or B12 deficiency) under their own topics. No dose was verified from a label here.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: All adults aged 65 years and over should be offered screening with a simple validated instrument (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 1).
Clinical assessment for everyone who screens positive for frailty or pre-frailty (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2).
Three or more of five components: weakness, slowness, shrinking, exhaustion, low physical activity (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2).
One or two of the five components (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 2).
Advanced (severe) frailty, where appropriate (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 4).

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale categories
diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Fit, vulnerable, mildly frail, moderately frail, severely frail; in 182 community-dwelling Saudis 61.5% were fit, 18.2% vulnerable, 13.7% mild, 4.95% moderate and 1.65% severe (Saudi Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale study, Section 3).

values: Preventive multicomponent exercise and risk factor review
Full care plan, medicines review, resistance exercise, nutrition, consider geriatrician

teaching.scope: Primary health centre doctors, nurses and allied health staff in Saudi Arabia screening adults aged 65 years and over for frailty, assessing those who screen positive, and building a care plan covering medicines review, exercise, nutrition, treatable causes of fatigue and weight loss, and referral to a geriatrician. Uses the International Conference of Frailty and Sarcopenia Research (ICFSR) guideline and a 2026 Saudi validation of the Arabic Edmonton Frail Scale. Not for acute illness or end-of-life care planning.
learningObjectives: Offer frailty screening to everyone aged 65 and over.
Three or more of five phenotype components means frail.
Check for treatable causes of tiredness and weight loss.
Review medicines and offer resistance-based exercise.
pitfalls: Treating each disease alone without a frailty care plan.
Giving vitamin D without a level.
keyPoints: Frailty is not the same as multimorbidity or disability.
Vitamin D only when deficiency is shown.

patientEducation: Frailty means your body has less reserve to cope with illness and stress. It can often be improved.
Regular exercise that includes strength training is the most useful treatment.
Eat enough protein and calories; tell us if you are losing weight without trying.
Bring all your medicines to each visit so we can see if any can be stopped.
Tell us about falls, low mood or memory problems.
lifestyleAndDiet: Join a group exercise programme or do home exercises with strength and balance.
Keep eating regular meals with protein.
Keep social contact with family and community.
Take care of your teeth and mouth.
mdtReferrals: Primary care doctor and nurse; geriatrician; pharmacist; physiotherapist; dietitian; social worker; dentist; family caregivers.
dischargeCriteria: Not applicable as a discharge: record the frailty category, care plan, medicine review outcome and review date.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review the care plan, function, weight and medicines at regular intervals; refer to a geriatrician if frailty advances (ICFSR frailty guideline, Recommendation 4).
